text: The last of the light was fading gold and pink.
Sunny watched the day tuck softly into night.
High on a branch, a chunky bird sat down,
with feathers brown and cream and soft and warm.
A kookaburra, king of all the laughs,
who chuckled loud across the bush all day.
But now his laugh was just a sleepy sound,
a soft “koo-koo” that faded into hush.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “Are you off to sleep?”
“I am,” he yawned. “The day is nearly done.”
He fluffed his feathers up into a ball
and tucked his beak beneath a cosy wing.
“I laughed all day,” he murmured, soft and low.
“Now it's time for quiet, time for rest.”
The bush grew still. The crickets softly sang.
The first star blinked above the darkening trees.
Sunny watched the kookaburra doze,
a round warm shape against the deep blue sky.
“Goodnight,” she whispered up into the tree.
“Goodnight,” he mumbled, half-asleep already.
Sunny found a mossy spot below
and curled up cosy in the gentle dark.
The night was warm. The moon was rising slow.
Everything was peaceful, still, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy as the stars came out.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath the sleeping bird,
both of them dreaming in the quiet night.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, kind kookaburra.
Goodnight, sleepy bush. Goodnight, little one.
